title: Consolidate console insights into minimal tiles with prioritized cost + trace telemetry
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Background:
We need a tight, production-friendly first pass of Console Insights that provides immediate value for customers (latency & cost visibility) while minimizing engineering surface area and instrumentation risk. This ticket records the PRD summary, scope trade-offs, and explicit acceptance criteria for the MVP cut.

Goals:
- Surface per-route latency percentiles, request rate, and top-5 cost contributors for the last 24h as compact dashboard tiles.
- Provide lightweight trace-sampling overview (sample rate indicator, top error spans) without a full flamegraph UX.
- Keep UI components re-usable and low-cardinality to reduce backend query load and cost.

Non-goals (MVP cuts):
- No full per-request flamegraphs or distributed trace timelines in MVP (postpone to trace-2).
- No unlimited cross-filters or ad-hoc query editor.
- No per-token cost attribution at launch; only route-level and model-variant aggregation.

PRD links and artifacts:
- Full PRD (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/insights/prd-minimal-tiles (internal)
- Figma mockups (MVP tiles set): https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Console-Insights-MVP
- Analytics dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console-insights/mvp-proto
- Design notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/insights-mvp-design

Why these cuts?
1) Engineering velocity: Removing flamegraphs and ad-hoc queries avoids additional tracing storage, high-cardinality indexes, and long-tail backend work.
2) Cost predictability: Limiting to top-5 contributors and 1m aggregation reduces Prometheus/Grafana query cost and retrieval latency.
3) Security & compliance: Smaller telemetry surface lowers risk for customers who require Private deployments.

Trade-offs and mitigations:
- Trade-off: Fewer interactive drilldowns reduces troubleshooting power.
  Mitigation: Add a clear CTA tile that exports a lightweight trace bundle for customer support (post-MVP troubleshoot).
- Trade-off: Aggregated cost may hide per-token anomalies.
  Mitigation: Include an opt-in deeper-export path (manual request) for power users in Dedicated/Private.

Acceptance criteria (must all be true for Done):
1) Dashboard tiles: "Latency (p50/p95)", "Requests/min", "Errors/min", "Top 5 cost contributors (route/model)", "Trace sampling rate" are implemented and visible for last 24h.
2) Each tile loads within 1.5s for customer with sample dataset (500k req/day) under staging infra.
3) Backend queries use 1m aggregation window by default and have documented query profiles for cost teams.
4) Top-5 cost calculation is reproducible and documented with test vectors (PR with unit tests).
5) Trace sampling tile shows current sample rate, sampled-error count, and links to exported traces; clicking export triggers a ticketed bundle generation.
6) No flamegraph or per-span waterfall UI shipped in this release (validated by QA checklist).
7) Product and Design signoff confirmed in Confluence PRD comment thread.
8) Dashboard includes 'Limitations' callout describing data latency, aggregation window, and known gaps.

Open questions (to be resolved before engineering kickoff):
- Do we store sampled traces longer than default retention for Paid customers? (Cost + compliance implications)
- What is the fallback UI behavior when metrics backend fails or exceeds quota? (Graceful degrade to last-known + warning)
- Should cost contributors include estimated GPU minutes or only token counts for MVP?

Decisions (agreed 2025-06-23):
- Keep trace storage at standard retention; do not extend retention for MVP. (Reason: cost & infra readiness)
- Use 1 minute aggregation for time-series tiles.
- For cost, surface both token-based cost and a simple estimated compute cost (GPU-min approximation) but only show top-5 entries.
- Export traces via a support-triggered async job; do not expose ad-hoc raw trace downloads in UI.

Tasks / next steps:
- PM -> finalize PRD and acceptance criteria (owner: Aisha)
- Design -> provide finalized Figma with responsive tiles and limitation callout (owner: Priya Kapoor)
- ENG -> estimate and break into backend queries / metrics pipeline / frontend tiles (owner: Marcus Li)
- ENG -> create sub-tickets: ENG-22456 (metrics-aggregation), ENG-22457 (trace-sample-summary), ENG-22458 (ui-tiles)

Review history and comments:
- 2025-06-18: Initial PRD summary created by Aisha Romero.
- 2025-06-20: Design feedback: request for explicit 'export' CTA; added to Acceptance criteria.
- 2025-06-22: Eng triage: recommended cutting flamegraph and per-request views; marked lower risk.
- 2025-06-23: Exec review: approved cuts for faster time-to-value; flagged cost estimator accuracy as follow-up.

QA & rollout plan:
- Staging rollout with canary to 5% of customers for one week. Verify load/latency and error trends.
- Run cost-sensitivity test for 3 synthetic workloads (100k, 500k, 2M req/day) and log query costs.
- Collect customer feedback via in-console survey after opt-in to canary.

Rollback criteria:
- Any tile consistently >3s load for production customers after rollout.
- Top-5 cost numbers deviate >30% from billing export for 2 consecutive days.
decisions: Cut flamegraph and per-request waterfall from MVP
Use 1m aggregation for all time-series tiles
Keep trace retention at default for MVP
Expose trace export as support-triggered async job only
acceptance_criteria: Five tiles implemented and visible (latency, rps, errors, top-5 cost, trace sampling)

Backend queries use documented 1m aggregation and pass unit tests
Top-5 cost calculation unit tests and docs present
No flamegraph UI shipped; QA checklist verifies absence
